spec_cite: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (source-address auth-failure rate exceeded -> Close(302); pairing failure rate -> Close(302))
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §10 (20 auth failures per sliding 60 s per source; 5 pairing failures; 8 outstanding requests)
description: Rate limiting: once a source address exceeds the failure budget, the Server answers with Close(302) (this vector shows the final Close; the budget buildup is precondition, not wire bytes).
preconditions: State machine: AUTHENTICATING; this source address has accumulated 20 auth failures (or 5 pairing failures) inside the sliding 60 s window.
The failure that trips the limit closes the connection.
assertions: Close(302) is sent as a frame here (unlike 301/601 — the §5.2 rows decide per case); the transport close carries the same code.
retryable=true per §6.2: the Client may reconnect with backoff, but the address stays throttled while failures continue.
No paired Error frame is specified by the §5.2 row for this path — the vector shows exactly Close(302).
